correctness.rationale: Every H-copy avoids any degree-one vertex by minimum degree >=2; conditional G(n-1,m-1) has exact hypergeometric motif moment. Combining the conditional and unconditional count identities yields R(1-e/m)-1 on e<=m<=B+1. Both zero cases and positivity of means are explicit. Monotonicity of the bracket yields the exhaustive sign classification, without assuming R>1. Expansion R=1+(2e-h)/n+O(n^-2), E[L]/n->2c exp(-2c), and the verified triangle algebra establish all asymptotics and sharp integer bounds. The actual standalone checker independently passed 163 exact exhaustive graph cells and 867049 exact sign cells, with triangle integer checks n=5..1000. These computations are evidence, not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The exact mixed covariance in the fixed-edge model with its all-motif shape-invariant sign diagram, exact triangle integer cutoff, and contrasting always-negative independent-edge law were not established by the inspected primary articles or closest retrieved mathematical records. The S&W article already gives the marginal fixed-edge motif expectation, and that is explicitly credited; the new dependence/classification goes beyond that marginal identity. Prior G(n,p) degree/motif covariance does not imply fixed-edge covariance because conditioning on total edge count changes edge dependence. Residual historical risk of an indirect factorial-moment derivation remains.
residual_risks: An older comprehensive mixed-factorial-moment formula for G(n,m) might imply the exact identity without using the terminology of leaves and motif covariance.

Scientific records and targeted literature searches cannot prove worldwide novelty or independence.

value.rationale: The dependence of pendant vertices on cyclic motifs is a natural mixed structural statistic of a sparse random graph. The fixed-edge ensemble produces a sharp positive regime despite the same covariance being negative for every p in the independent-edge ensemble. The exact integer triangle boundary m=n versus m=n+1, universal fixed-motif critical density e/(2e-h), and dependence only on the motif vertex/edge counts form a motivated complete classification; they are not just generic covariance identities or single arbitrary numerical cases. The known marginal motif expectation alone does not answer this question.
